allocations.exactDerivedText: Anthropic is easing Claude’s biology restrictions for vetted research teams
Anthropic announced its Life Sciences Verification Program on September 17.
The beta gives verified life-science teams versions of Claude that allow more biology requests than general Claude.
Teams and institutions come first; individual Pro and Max access is planned later.
Applicants are reviewed for research credentials, security and ethical oversight.

Anthropic says the program is designed for life-science work that general Claude blocks. The closest alternative is general Claude with stricter biology restrictions; special access is unnecessary when an ordinary request already works there.
Standard Use covers a team and renews yearly.
High-risk Use is an extra six-month grant for one project that removes life-science request blocks.
Anthropic says LSVP replaces immediate refusals with looking for patterns after activity runs.
Access is tied to an approved use case. The company says it keeps LSVP traffic for 30 days so monitoring can happen.
This changes access for vetted research institutions, not your personal Claude account.
Anthropic loosened some biology blocks for vetted institutional teams, while replacing immediate refusals with monitored, scoped access.
Anthropic — Introducing the Life Sciences Verification Program
